summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, morbid obesity, and chronic venous stasis ulcers was admitted for worsening bilateral leg pain and weeping ulcers. She was found to have acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema, likely due to fluid and sodium overload, requiring IV diuresis and oxygen support. Her kidney function transiently worsened but improved with treatment. Poor heart rate control led to adjustment of her beta-blocker regimen. Chronic respiratory acidosis persisted but stabilized. Wound care was intensified with frequent dressing changes. Asymptomatic bacteriuria with multidrug-resistant E. coli was noted but not treated. She was transitioned to a sliding scale insulin regimen for glucose management. After clinical improvement, she was discharged to extended care rehabilitation with stable vital signs and optimized medical management.
